findings.title: TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar (now a common case: handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one). The very next line dereferences it unconditionally: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and aborts `EventManager.create()` for any Google Meet booking made by a user without a destination calendar. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for non-calendar (video) results; the previous code used `result.credentialId` in that branch. Video meeting references are therefore persisted with `credentialId: null`. Cancellation logic depends on it: `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy (see packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts ~line 491), so Zoom/MS Teams/etc. meetings will silently stop being deleted when a booking is cancelled.

findings.title: updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId
findings.body: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` are read from the results of `updateAllCalendarEvents`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-323) does not return `externalId` or `credentialId` at all — only `createEvent` was changed to return them. Previously these values came from `evt.destinationCalendar`. As a result, every booking reference created by an "edit location" action loses its calendar linkage, and subsequent updates/cancellations can no longer resolve the right credential/calendar (they fall back to iterating all credentials or to "primary").

findings.title: Organization slug assignment logic inverted
findings.body: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the previous condition `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The intent is: when billing is enabled the slug is only *requested* (stored in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment), otherwise the slug is set directly. With this change, a billing-enabled instance sets both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug`, and a non-billing instance (self-hosted) creates the organization with **no slug at all**, so org subdomain resolution/`orgDomains` lookups break for newly created orgs. This change is also unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the ternary's else branch), so it compares each `cal.externalId` against `undefined`/`""` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Consequently, when no external calendar id is passed, `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined })` is issued instead of targeting the destination calendar, and the update fails. The intent was presumably to fall back to the first (main host) destination calendar.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: Same self-defeating condition as in `updateEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always resolves to `undefined` and the code silently falls back to `"primary"`. Previously it used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Events stored in a non-primary destination calendar will therefore not be found/deleted (Google returns 404, which the handler swallows), leaving orphaned calendar events after cancellations.

findings.title: createEvent ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` explicitly handles that case by calling `createEvent(credential, event)` without an externalId. For those rows the `find` returns `undefined` and the event is created in `"primary"` instead of the user's configured destination calendar — a regression from the previous `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. A fallback to the destination calendar matching this integration (or the first one) is needed.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch sends calendarId: undefined
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` uses `selectedCalendar` directly, but `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (the `|| "primary"` default was moved to the insert call only). When the destination calendar can't be resolved, the insert succeeds against `primary` while the patch that adds the Meet link to the description is sent with no calendarId and fails.

findings.title: Duplicate calendar events created for multiple destination calendars without credentialId
findings.body: For each destination with no `credentialId`, the code filters *all* of the organizer's credentials of that integration type and creates an event with each. With the new multi-destination array (e.g. two collective hosts both having a Google destination calendar with `credentialId: null`), this loop runs once per destination using the same credential set, producing N duplicate events in the same calendar. The per-destination branch should create at most one event for the destination it is iterating over.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents error message computed but never logged
findings.body: The catch block still builds the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed in this change. Calendar update failures are now swallowed entirely with no log output, making production debugging of failed reschedules/updates impossible.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, and `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case all the collected host destination calendars are discarded, so collective hosts get no calendar invite — exactly the scenario this PR aims to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) before pushing, or build the array in one expression.

findings.title: Dynamic-booking user select no longer fetches organization slug
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the `prisma.user.findMany` select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings. This field was added deliberately for org-aware booker URLs; without it any downstream use of `user.organization?.slug` resolves to undefined (or fails type-checking because the two branches of `loadUsers` now return different shapes), producing wrong links for dynamic group bookings in organizations. The removal is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor.

findings.title: Empty dynamicUserList surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400
findings.body: `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is a plain `Error`, so the catch below (which only re-wraps `HttpError` and Prisma errors as 400) converts it into `HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed/empty client-supplied user list is a client error and previously did not produce a 5xx; this will pollute error monitoring and give the booker no useful message.

findings.title: Recurring-cancellation deletion repeated once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring + `allRemainingBookings` block (which itself loops over every user calendar credential and every updated booking) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With multiple calendar references (the normal case for the new multi-host destination calendars) the same delete calls are issued refs × credentials × bookings times, multiplying external API calls against Google/Office and relying on 404/410 swallowing for correctness. The recurring branch should run once, outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar shape is now inconsistent (null vs []) and breaking for consumers
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` in the webhook payload changes from an object/null to an array, but the code paths are inconsistent: BOOKING_REJECTED/confirm now emits `[]` (this assertion), while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still assert `null` (lines 119 and 373) because handleNewBooking sets `null` when there is no destination calendar. External webhook consumers parsing `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break, and they now have to handle three shapes (object-less array, empty array, null). The shape should be normalized (always an array) and the payload change documented as breaking.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent credentialId made a required parameter
findings.body: `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` adds a required second parameter to the public `Calendar` interface. Any caller outside of `CalendarManager` (other packages/apps, third-party calendar app implementations in the app store that are invoked directly) that calls `createEvent(evt)` now fails type-checking, and at runtime receives `undefined` for `credentialId` — which in GoogleCalendarService makes the destination-calendar lookup fail and silently writes to `primary`. Making the parameter optional and defensively handling `undefined` would avoid both the contract break and the silent misrouting.
